title: Estimated Sparse Fourier Hypothesis
statement: Given a deterministic Goldreich–Levin input, a finite family of frequency sets in the input dimension, and a sign-valued answer for each sample in the input's coefficient-estimation sample set, define a sparse Fourier hypothesis supported on that family, with each coefficient given by the rational small-bias Fourier estimate for the corresponding frequency set.
hypotheses_covered: The input's small-bias parameters have positive dimension and numerator, with twice the numerator at most the denominator.
The Fourier bound is a natural number at least one.
The family is a finite set of frequency sets in the input dimension.
One sign-valued answer is supplied for each coefficient-estimation sample.
caveat: The supplied statement does not include the definitions of the coefficient input, sample count, rational estimator, or coefficient-based hypothesis constructor, so the coefficient rule cannot be made more explicit.
